title: ADAS Sensor Calibrations Desk Guidance: The Record Date a No-Show Is Measured To
content:
The record date the no-show is measured to on an ADAS Sensor Calibrations customer-pay calibration follows how the order arose:

- for an order opened on the **customer's own request**, it is the order's opening date;
- for an order opened on a **network customer-pay repair**, it is that repair's opening date, as recorded on the Customer-Pay Repairs order;
- for **any other order**, it is the day of the acceptance.

## Records that fix the record date

| How the order arose (the order's recorded source) | Record date | Record read |
|---|---|---|
| Customer request | The calibration order's opening date | The calibration order |
| Network customer-pay repair | The opening date of the source customer-pay repair | The Customer-Pay Repairs order the calibration order was opened on |
| Glass replacement, collision repair, warranty rework | The day the customer accepts the calibration | The day of acceptance |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A calibration order opened on the customer's own request on 4 June and accepted on 9 June: the record date is 4 June.
- A calibration order opened on 4 June on a network customer-pay repair that was opened on 28 May, accepted on 9 June: the record date is 28 May.
- A calibration order opened after a glass replacement and accepted on 9 June: the record date is 9 June.
